newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FOCUS-EMU DELAY PERHAPS WARRENTED - SCHROEDER.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-EMU DELAY PERHAPS WARRENTED - SCHROEDER.

text.p: German Social Democrat Gerhard Schroeder, a leading candidate to challenge Chancellor Helmut Kohl in 1998 elections, suggested in a newspaper interview on Wednesday that Europe's single currency may have to be delayed.

"If it is possible to introduce the euro in 1999 with a stability-orientated policy, then good. If it cannot be done without grinding economic, social and political damage, then you have to chose a more favourable time," he told Switzerland's Finanz und Wirtschaft business newspaper.
Schroeder, premier of Lower Saxony state, said he did not consider Economic and Monetary Union to be superfluous or see himself as a Eurosceptic.

"I am for Europe. But I remind you that the common currency was once seen as the culmination of European unity. We were supposed to introduce it when the economic and social union was completed," he was quoted as saying.
"Today we are still far removed from harmonised tax and
social policy or environmental standards, but we are in a great hurry with the euro."
Kohl has backed strict adherence to both the tough
economic criteria founding members of the euro must meet and to the timetable for introducing the single currency.
But opposition leader Oskar Lafontaine said on Monday he
believed a strict insistence on holding budget deficits to 3.0 percent of gross domestic product -- one of the key membership rules -- was "economic nonsense".
